The SuperUnicode Standard

Base SUCS — a 31-bit character system of codepoints, machine instructions and a permanent Unicode bridge.

The Base SuperUnicode Character System (SUCS) occupies the codepoint space 0x00000000–0x7FFFFFFF (31 significant bits, held in a uint32_t SUCS_CP). Everything the standard defines is documented here and in the machine-instruction database.

Core invariants

  • SUCS_CP is 31-bit; sucs_ex_char_t is 64-bit.
  • 0x000000–0x10FFFF is permanently 1:1 with Unicode.
  • 0x7FFFFFFF is the Sentinel; no allocation exists at or below it.
  • Plugin codepoints start strictly above 0x7FFFFFFF and mount only after the boot checksum gate.

See also: the machine-instruction database (the data behind these rules) and SUTR-0 — SUCS Core (the normative report).
